newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices extend losses on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices extend losses on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices continued their downward spiral Monday as mild temperatures in the central U.S. dissuaded buyers from the marketplace, sources said.

Prices on the Gulf Coast pipes fell by about 60 cents to the $3.20s as Northeast buyers relied on plentiful storage inventories to meet heating demand and mild temperatures dampened demand in the southern plains and Midwest.
Similarly in south Texas prices plummeted by about 70 cents to the $2.90s, down about a $1 from week-ago levels.

In the Midcontinent, where temperatures were expected to be about 10-15 degrees Fahrenheit above-normal Tuesday and Wednesday, prices dropped by more than 65 cents to about $2.90, erasing about $1.30 from index levels.
Chicago city-gate values were talked mostly in the $3.25-3.30 range.
In west Texas, Permian prices fell by about 50-55 cents to the $2.74-2.79 range, with deals reported done anywhere from $2.65 to $3.09.
In the East, where stocks are well above year-ago levels, prices cratered into the low-$4 area, down about 30 cents from index levels.
